#4657. In 1841, flesh and blood rained down in Tennessee

Published Oct 30, 2026 1:53 PM EDT

One August day in 1841, near Lebanon, Tennessee, two enslaved people heard the sound of rain pattering on the tobacco leaves around them. But this was no ordinary rain: It was a deep red color. The sky, it seemed, was raining blood. Even more alarming, small pieces of flesh and fat seemed to be raining down, too. The two witnesses took the leaves inside to show their enslaver, Mr. E.M. Chandler, who quickly reported the event to his neighbors.

In an attempt to clear things up, pieces of fallen material were sent to Dr. Gerard Troost, a renowned scientist and collector of natural history specimens. Upon opening the package, Troost noted that it “had the offensive smell of putrid animal matter.” After a thorough analysis, Dr. Troost’s assessment was clear: “There is no doubt but that this substance is animal matter and belongs to our globe.”

The flesh and blood fall near Lebanon in 1841 was far from the only time blood rain or flesh has fallen from the sky, nor was it the last. Both experts and lay people have put forward various explanations for blood rains and flesh falls, including animals being torn up by storms, hoaxes, carcasses dropped by vultures, meteor dust, algal spores, or even red discharge from butterflies.

The 1841 blood rain incident in Lebanon has to be contextualized within the buildup to the Civil War, and a massacre that happened almost exactly 10 years earlier. In 1831, an enslaved carpenter and preacher named Nat Turner in Southampton, Virginia began having visions of “lights in the sky to which the children of darkness gave other names than what they really were—for they were the lights of the Saviour’s hands,” followed by sightings of “drops of blood on the corn, as though it were dew from heaven.”

When Turner later found hieroglyphic marks written in blood on leaves in the woods, he took it as an omen: Shortly afterwards, he led one of the deadliest uprisings of enslaved people in U.S. history. From August 21 to August 23, 1831, Nat Turner and his followers killed 55 white people. In response, local militias and roving mobs killed an unknown number of both enslaved and free Black people. Nat Turner and some of his followers were sentenced to death and executed.

When enslaved people discovered blood on the tobacco leaves in Lebanon in 1841, the fuss was enormous, and echoed Nat Turner’s accounts of bloody rain. Locals in Lebanon wrote about their local blood rain incident in letters to relatives, newspapers from near and far reported on it, and the farm became somewhat of a circus.

A visitor from another town, William F. Cooper, wrote in his journal that “the smell of this fallen matter was very offensive, polluting the whole air.” Cooper also described the extent of the fall as “from 40 to 60 yards in width, and six or eight hundred yards in length,” equivalent to around six to eight football fields.

After Dr. Troost later analyzed the material and determined it was, in fact, animal matter, the flesh fall was reported in the American Journal of Science. Troost’s primary theory was that a strong wind “might have taken up part of an animal which was in a state of decomposition, and have brought it in contact with an electric cloud, in which it was kept in a state of partial fluidity or viscosity.”

After the Lebanon flesh and blood fall, stories of Nat Turner and the slave rebellion were revived in full force. Many white Southerners feared another uprising. On the other hand, Northerners saw the blood rain as a heavenly critique on the practice of slavery.

On September 10, 1841, The Wisconsin Enquirer reported that residents in Northern states had likened the Lebanon event to the blood fall in Virginia that occurred before Nat Turner’s uprising, and “construed the mysterious shower [in Lebanon] into a judgment from heaven, designed to warn the slave-holding states of the iniquity of their traffic in flesh and blood.”

The mystery of the flesh and blood fall in Lebanon was never totally resolved, and was eventually dismissed as a hoax perpetrated by the two enslaved people who witnessed it first. This was later rebutted in The Western Journal of Medicine and Surgery in December 1841.

“People have a need for an explanation, just any explanation, regardless of whether or not it is the explanation,” says Tom Maxwell, writer, blood rain researcher, and host of The Night Parade podcast. “In this case, I think culturally a lot of people needed it to be a hoax.”

Blood rains and flesh falls stretch far back into history. They are mentioned in both The Iliad and the Bible. Philosophers, scientists, and storytellers have described numerous incidents throughout the centuries, including in ancient Rome, medieval Ireland, the 19th century United States, and around the world today.

Nineteenth-century scientists even attempted to find a scientific reason for these falls with microscopes. These scientists could determine “it was always blood. It was always animal material,” says Maxwell. “The question was how did it get where it got, not what it was.” Contemporary scientists have narrowed in on these two separate questions: First, what is falling from the sky, and second, how did it get in the sky?

While blood rains and flesh falls are often discussed together, there are likely different mechanisms behind them. One common explanation for flesh falls lines up with what Troost proposed in 1841: a strong storm, or even vultures, can sweep flesh up into the sky and drop it down later. Strange weather events like this are not unheard of, and fish falls, insect tornadoes, or even frogs falling from the sky have all been documented before.

Blood rain, on the other hand, has a completely different explanation. In these cases, the rain is red because it likely contains dust or microorganisms rather than animal matter. This was hard to detect in the past.

“They didn’t have the science,” says Dr. Patrick McCafferty, a researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology who has studied how myths and literature often record real-world comets, meteor strikes, or other catastrophes. “So [from their perspective] this seems to be something sent by God to punish them.”

The reality is that since Christians were largely familiar with the concept of an impending doomsday and blood rain in the Bible, “They would interpret these things as blood,” says McCafferty. “They’re also primed to look out for these signs of the end of the world.”

Bloody rains studied in the past few decades have given clues as to what the substance may be, at least in some cases. One key example of this is the blood rain that fell in Kerala, India, in 2001.

Researchers collected samples of the red rain, and found it contained algal or seaweed spores, which caused the red coloration. Another research group argued the Kerala blood rain was the result of dust blown over from desert areas in West Asia.

Yet another group asserted that the Kerala blood rain was red because it was full of “bacteria-like material that had been swept to Earth from a passing comet.” They argued that if a comet had broken apart in the Earth’s atmosphere, extraterrestrial particles could have made it into the clouds, raining down as blood-red droplets.

Despite the frequent co-occurrence of meteors or comets and blood rain (a route of investigation also pursued by McCafferty) the explanation has not been widely adopted.

With so many eyewitness accounts of blood rains and flesh falls across the centuries, it’s hard to dismiss the phenomenon. “Chances are, it was real. Chances are, it was caused by something,” says McCafferty. “I’m conscious that things happen that do not have a good explanation.”

When it comes to meat, fat, or red rain falling from the sky, we shouldn’t be too quick to dismiss what it really looks like: flesh and blood. “The classic example is the [French Academy of Sciences] completely dismissing accounts that stones fell from the sky,” says McCafferty.

“So when anybody would come to them with a meteorite, they would say ‘This was hit by thunder or this was hit by lightning. This is a thunderstone. It was hit by lightning. It did not fall from space. It’s stupid to believe stones fall from space.’ And then it turns out that, oh, actually they do.”

Many questions about blood rain and flesh falls remain unanswered. In Maxwell’s opinion, that’s okay: “In the face of the inexplicable,” he says, “I think the most appropriate epistemological response is ‘I don’t know.’”

#4656. New retro electric motorcycle to debut at EICMA with a novel feature: a second gear

Most electric motorcycles have something in common: a single-speed transmission. But a British company is preparing to shake things up at this year’s EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, where it will unveil a new electric motorcycle demonstrator featuring an unusual two-speed transmission designed to shift gears without interrupting power delivery.

The company behind the technology, E-Motiv Shift Systems, has developed what it calls a seamless powershift transmission, promising improved acceleration, better efficiency, and a more engaging riding experience.

Unlike conventional motorcycle transmissions, which generally require a brief interruption in power during gear changes, E-Motiv’s system is designed to maintain torque throughout the shift.

That could offer some interesting advantages for electric motorcycles, where a lower first gear could provide stronger acceleration while a taller second gear could help optimize motor efficiency at higher speeds.

Of course, most electric motorcycles don’t actually need multiple gears, and very few have ever offered multi-speed transmissions. Electric motors produce strong torque across a wide operating range, which is why manufacturers generally prefer the simplicity, lower weight, and reduced maintenance of single-speed drivetrains.

But that doesn’t mean a second gear couldn’t offer some benefits.

E-Motiv’s technology actually traces its roots back nearly 25 years to the Zeroshift transmission system, which eventually found its way into Aprilia’s MotoGP racing motorcycles in 2015.

It's possible, from my perspective, that running a motor at lower rpm under reduced load like flat terrain cruising, could improve range, and lower temperatures, and might be beneficial for cars and trucks as well.

The latest electric version was developed through a £1 million UK government-funded project involving motorcycle manufacturer BSA, the University of Bath, and the Institute of Advanced Automotive Propulsion Systems (IAAPS).

The demonstrator motorcycle, known as Demo 1, was conceived by British design consultancy Envisage and is being built by IAAPS. Real-world testing is scheduled to begin in early 2027.

E-Motiv will showcase the technology at EICMA from November 3-8, though the demonstrator remains a development project rather than a production-ready motorcycle.

Whether two-speed transmissions eventually become common on electric motorcycles remains to be seen. But if E-Motiv can deliver meaningful efficiency and performance improvements without adding too much weight, cost, or complexity, it could give future electric motorcycles another interesting trick up their sleeves.

#4654. Kia Says Too Much Technology Is Taking the Fun Out of Driving

Kia's Telluride Is Closing In On The Sportage's U.S. Sales Crown

Ford Crams The Most Powerful OEM Crate Engine Ever Made Into New Bronco Concept

Mercedes-Benz Wants To Blow Snow Off Your Car Before You Open The Door

Kia believes that even everyday cars should be enjoyable behind the wheel, as it reckons good-driving cars are thinning out.

Cadillac Escalade IQ Has a Suspension Squeak With No Fix Yet

This 800-HP Ford F-100 Has Mustang DNA and a $1 Million Price Tag

Winter Weather Advisory Issued for Up to 11 Inches of Snow Across Colorado Through Thursday

You don’t always need an overtly sporty car to enjoy great driving dynamics. Even regular cars can be fun behind the wheel, bringing some joy to one’s everyday commute. Some shining examples include the Mazda3 and Honda Civic, while moving up the price bracket, you have compact executive sedans like the Alfa Romeo Giulia and BMW 3 Series.

Still, the list isn’t long enough, reckons Kia, as its chief ride and handling engineer for Australia, Graeme Gambold, said driving enthusiasts are being overlooked. He also mentioned that technology, while good, has been taking away the fun element in cars.

Speaking to Australian motoring publication Carsales, Gambold expressed his frustration towards some driver assist technologies. “It’s really hard to find a car that drives nicely. It’s really hard to find a car that has all the features but none of the safety intervention, as I don’t need it,” said the engineer.

Now, that’s a pretty bold statement from a company chief, especially since automakers are committed to advanced driver assist technologies. He’s not saying that those should be banned altogether, as there have been instances wherein these were genuine lifesavers. Instead, it’s the intrusiveness of these systems that annoys instead of giving joy.

Carsales also asked Gambold if fun cars are a dying art. While he said it wasn’t necessarily the case, he stated that current market priorities have put enthusiasts aside. It’s one of the reasons why Kia (along with Hyundai) still has ride and handling tuning divisions in its major markets. In an age where everyone is trying to shave chunks of cost, the South Korean automaker is more than willing to spend on catering its chassis to specific markets.

Right now, the main priority seems to be pushing out new models at lightning speed. It’s something that the Chinese market has effectively pressured legacy automakers to do, particularly in the fields of technology and electrification. But while higher-end models come with tricky suspension arrangements, one has to wonder how these cars would actually fare without these. It’s possible that electronics could be masking what are, otherwise, shortcomings in basic chassis tuning.

That’s the rub of the more widespread availability of active and adaptive suspension systems. While it’s good that the trickle-down effect has made these reasonably-priced options, it does make chassis engineering more tech-dependent, which also adds a layer of complexity to any vehicle. As China has effectively pressured the world into developing cars faster, and a majority of car buyers simply want point A to B transport, it doesn’t really encourage automakers to add a little zing to their mass-market models.

Of course, there may come a time when cars can be completely software-defined. Many automakers aren’t exactly shy about going in that direction. Still, at least we know some brands still see value in proper chassis tuning and calibration rather than just letting active systems and software development do a good chunk of the work.

#4653. Ford casts 5,000 ‘unicastings’ for Fathom EV truck in Tesla-style shift

Ford has now produced more than 5,000 large aluminum “unicastings” for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch.

Each truck gets two of them, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts. It’s the clearest sign yet that Ford is all-in on the manufacturing approach Tesla popularized with its Giga Press six years ago.

The update comes from Vladimir Bogachuk, Ford’s chief engineer of advanced vehicle structure architecture, in a post on Ford’s From the Road blog. The castings are made at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center and shipped to Louisville Assembly Plant for process testing and prototype builds. Louisville is the Kentucky factory Ford is retooling for the Fathom and other vehicles on its Universal EV Platform.

Ford melts aluminum ingots at about 1,300°F (700°C) and injects the metal into either a front or rear structure mold. Once a robot pulls the part out, it goes into a quench tank, gets trimmed and machined, and then runs a gauntlet of checks: industrial X-ray scans for pores and voids, dimensional measurements in a climate-controlled room, optical surface scans, and lab tensile and chemistry tests on samples.

Nothing ships to Louisville until a batch clears every inspection. Ford says it’s also working on cutting cycle time and on designing the castings for “modular repairability.”

That last part has been the main reason why automakers have been reticent about larger cast parts. Repair cost is the biggest knock on giant castings, since a damaged one-piece structure can turn a moderate crash into a write-off. Lucid executive Cory Steuben has said insurance concerns drove the company’s decision to skip gigacasting altogether.

Tesla kicked this off in 2020 with the first IDRA Giga Press at Fremont, a machine with roughly 6,000 tons of clamping force. It cast the Model Y’s rear underbody in a single piece, replacing 70 parts, and Elon Musk said the change removed the need for about 300 robots.

Tesla wanted to go much further. It added a front casting, tied the two together with a structural battery pack, and moved to even bigger presses for the Cybertruck. But in 2024, Reuters reported that Tesla had backed away from its plan to cast nearly the entire underbody in one piece, and the automaker has reportedly since dropped the front casting on some Model Y production.

So Ford’s 146-to-2 figure looks great on paper. But it’s a front-and-rear layout, basically the same architecture Tesla launched with on the Model Y. Ford isn’t leapfrogging Tesla here. It’s catching up, just with a vehicle that will cost less than any Tesla on sale.

Since that first Giga Press, a growing list of automakers have bought huge presses or committed to them:

Anyone have real world experience with how much the cost of repairability with Tesla Gigacasting? As mentioned in article likely to get totaled by insurance and/or expensive to fix compared to the traditional modular approach, shifting cost to consumer to reduce corporate costs.

Others aren’t buying it. Stellantis has said it won’t invest in gigacasting, while BMW and Mercedes-Benz have stuck with smaller presses for body parts. Hyundai pushed its “Hypercasting” plan back two years.

We’ve been tracking this casting race since Tesla’s first Giga Press showed up in Fremont, and the lesson so far is simple. Fewer parts is great, but the press alone doesn’t make a car cheap. The whole factory does.

That’s why Ford’s approach is worth watching. The unicastings are one piece of a bigger overhaul at Louisville, where Ford is splitting the line into three branches (front, rear, and the battery pack with the interior floor) that meet at the end. Ford says that can be up to 40% faster than its current assembly, or about 15% net once it reinvests some of the savings into automation and insourcing. It’s very close to the logic behind Tesla’s “unboxed” process, and they are betting it’s what actually gets you to a $28,350 truck.

#4652. Send your name to Saturn’s largest moon

Published Oct 30, 2026 2:34 PM EDT

NASA is still on track to send its Dragonfly rotocraft to Saturn’s moon Titan by the end of the decade, and you can come along for the ride. Well, you can at least add your initials to the flight roster.

As part of its Journey to Titan campaign, NASA has opened an online registry that will be included on a microchip aboard the spacecraft when it launches. The launch is currently scheduled for no earlier than July 2028. Signees will receive a personalized digital “boarding pass,” as proof that their names will reach the ice-encased Saturnian moon in 2034. While the encoded autographs may not do much to help with the overall mission, it’s nice to know that you will be represented on what may become one of the most consequential space endeavors of all time.

“We are excited to bring humanity along for the journey of a lifetime, and we invite everyone to send their names on this small, but mighty rotorcraft that will unlock the secrets of the universe,” Nicky Fox, NASA’s Science Mission Directorate associate administrator, said in the announcement.

Titan is the largest of Saturn’s 292 known moons, and a longtime dream destination in the search for life beyond Earth. Although Titan features dusty dunes overlooking lakes and rivers of methane, the frigid surface also maintains a temperature of around −290 degrees Fahrenheit. This is inhospitable to life as we know it, but a giant ocean also exists beneath the icy shell. Astrobiologists widely agree that these waters probably contain enough complex compounds to facilitate a prebiotic environment. Laboratory simulations of Titan’s atmosphere have also indicated its gaseous conditions can even form some of the principle building blocks for DNA and RNA. If true, extraterrestrial microbial life may exist within the moon’s hidden waters.

However, there’s no way to confirm the possibility without directly examining Titan’s conditions. That’s where Dragonfly comes into play. After over six years of interplanetary travel, NASA’s eight-bladed robotic rotocraft will land on the moon and begin its environmental survey. Dragonfly’s vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capabilities will allow it to travel to multiple locations over the planned three-year mission. If all goes well, the rotocraft will journey across 70 miles on Titan, while visiting 20 to 30 different areas.

“By flying the first-ever rotorcraft science mission, NASA will…we search for signs of habitability on a distant world that is most similar to our own,” added Fox.

Dragonfly is currently under construction at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland. It marks the fourth mission in NASA’s New Frontiers Program, which is dedicated to further exploration of the planets and moons that comprise our solar system.

Adding your name to Dragonfly’s log is likely a no-brainer for many people, but there is no rush if you need to take some time to ponder the decision. Signees have until 11:59 p.m. EST on January 15, 2027, to make their (digital) mark.

#4651. Kimi Antonelli is F1’s Newest Champion

With his Podium finish in the Mexico City Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli secures his spot as F1’s youngest champion.

Twelve championships stand on the podium following the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix as Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest F1 Champion in sports history with a third-place finish in Mexico City.

The 20-year-old Italian needed only a ninth-place finish in the Mexico City Grand Prix to win the championship, but that wasn’t enough for him or Mercedes, as the team went on to secure it with a podium finish behind the Four-time and Seven-time champions.

Antonelli finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix, joining Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton on the podium the driver that Mercedes missed out on to start Toto Wolff’s vindetta to find the future of the sport, and the legendary driver that Kimi replaced.

“We did it,” Antonelli told F1TV. “And without them, I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family. So I'm very grateful for this moment, and it's one that will live forever. And I'm speechless. I am trying to process what has just happened.

“It's been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max and Lewis is truly incredible. And yeah, looking forward to some more battles in the future.”

The year started with Mercedes dominance as teams struggled to catch up in the development race under the new 2026 regulations. What looked to be a battle between him and his senior teammate became a runaway train for Antonelli, who won five in a row early and then pulled out championship-level drives when the rest of the field started to catch up, including in his 19th-to-first run at his home Grand Prix where he became the first Italian driver to win at home since Ludovico Scarfiotti.

Through 19th rounds, Kimi Antonelli won nine races and finished on the podium in 16 races to secure the championship with four races remaining on the calendar.

He did all of this in his second season in F1, just five years after graduating from karts to car racing.

#4650. Tesla confirms Vietnam entry to take on VinFast and its 36% market share

Tesla has started hiring in Vietnam, and one of its recruiters says the company is now “officially coming” to the country. The five open roles include a sales manager, a service manager, and a charging project developer.

It’s a tough market to walk into. VinFast, the local all-electric automaker, has sold roughly 36% of every new car in Vietnam this year, more than its next five competitors combined.

Tesla quietly registered Tesla Motors Vietnam LLC in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11, with about 77.7 billion dong (roughly $3 million) in charter capital and a business scope covering car imports, wholesale, and retail. Tesla never commented on it.

Now we have the first confirmation from someone inside the company. Ricky Ip, who recruits for Tesla, posted on X this morning:

Tesla is officially coming to Vietnam – and we're hiring.Our mission is to build a world of amazing abundance and we are looking for passionate people to join us in Vietnam and help make that vision a reality. Current Job Openings:Sales Manager – https://t.co/AvW3higssS… pic.twitter.com/YDZvLNmz8P

The five openings are Sales Manager, Service Manager, HR Business Partner, Purchasing Manager, and Project Developer, Charging. That last one is the tell. You don’t hire someone to develop charging projects unless you plan to build Superchargers in the country.

Tesla has followed this playbook before in Southeast Asia. It went on a hiring spree in Thailand in September 2022 and opened orders there three months later. It started hiring in the Philippines in September 2024 and launched in early 2025. So a Vietnam launch in the next few months wouldn’t be a surprise.

There’s no word yet on pricing, models, or store locations. Oddly, the recruiting graphic features the next-generation Roadster, with fine print saying the vehicle is “for illustration purposes only.” Fair enough.

Tesla isn’t walking into an empty market. It’s walking into VinFast’s backyard.

VinFast delivered 177,697 cars in Vietnam through the first nine months of 2026, out of a national total of about 495,000. That’s about 36% of the entire car market, gas cars included. In September alone, it had 37.7% of the market.

Here’s how the year-to-date numbers stack up against the next brands:

Add up Toyota, Hyundai, Mitsubishi, Ford, and Kia and you get 175,136. VinFast alone beat all five of them.

And it’s already passed its full-year 2025 volume with a quarter left to go. VinFast says September was its 25th straight month as Vietnam’s best-selling car brand.

The model mix tells you a lot about the market. The VinFast VF 3, a tiny two-door electric crossover that launched at under $13,000, is Vietnam’s best-selling vehicle so far this year. VinFast models held the top five spots in September.

VinFast builds its cars in Haiphong. Tesla would have to import everything, most likely from Giga Shanghai, and Vietnam kept passenger cars on its high-tariff list under the ASEAN-China free trade agreement.

Expanding to Vietnam is a logical step considering the other markets nearby that Tesla is already selling in. In these markets, a smaller and affordable car (model 2) would have been a big seller.

Charging is another gap. VinFast’s sister company V-Green runs the country’s dominant charging network and announced plans this year to spend about $380 million on 99 ultra-fast charging stations. Third-party networks in Vietnam are still thin.

There is one thing working in Tesla’s favor. Vietnam just extended its registration fee exemption for battery-electric cars through the end of 2030, and that applies to imported EVs too.

And VinFast’s volume comes with an asterisk. A significant share of its deliveries go to GSM, the Xanh SM electric taxi and ride-hailing company founded by VinFast chairman Pham Nhat Vuong. VinFast has long relied on Vietnam for the bulk of its deliveries, which we pointed out when it delivered nearly 100,000 EVs in 2024.

A 1997 Ferrari F50 showing just 106 original miles recently sold for $17 million. This transaction establishes a new public pricing record for the 1990s Italian supercar, reflecting a sustained secondary market demand for ultra-low mileage collector vehicles. As automotive investors increasingly target analog supercars from this specific era, the financial benchmark for pristine Maranello halo cars continues to shift upward.

This specific chassis is the exact vehicle we reported earlier when it first became available to the public. While initial industry estimates boldly suggested the supercar might surpass the $20 million mark, the $17 million closing price still comfortably exceeds all previous public sales figures. It secures the vehicle’s position as one of the most valuable modern Ferraris in existence, bridging the historical gap between the turbocharged F40 and the technologically advanced Enzo.

According to a recent post on the Hagerty Instagram page, this chassis stands as one of the lowest-mileage F50s in existence. The vehicle spent the last two decades secured in a climate-controlled collection, effectively preserving its factory-delivered condition and maximizing its appeal to high-end buyers. In the elite collector car market, an unblemished, 106-mile odometer reading from 1997 transforms a vehicle from a mere sports car into a heavily scrutinized blue-chip asset.

F50 valuations have climbed steadily over the last decade as collectors recognize the rarity of the analog driving experience. While earlier examples sold for significantly less, even when carrying notable celebrity ownership, current market dynamics have fundamentally changed. Today’s serious automotive investors place a substantially higher financial premium on absolute delivery-mileage preservation and mechanical originality rather than focusing on a vehicle’s specific ownership history or famous previous drivers.

Ferrari originally engineered the F50 to celebrate the company’s 50th anniversary, purposefully utilizing a naturally aspirated 4.7-liter V12 engine derived directly from its 1990 Formula 1 racing program. Pushing 512 horsepower through a traditional six-speed manual transmission, the carbon-fiber chassis famously lacked power steering, power brakes, and modern stability control. Because the automaker strictly capped total global production at just 349 units, any surviving F50 remains an exceptionally rare acquisition on the open market.

To command top market value at this elite financial level, a collector-grade F50 must include absolutely all of its original accessories. This specific sale meticulously included the factory flight cases, the removable hardtop with its dedicated stand, the soft top, and the matching customized luggage. Maintaining these rare factory gems is strictly required to fully authenticate a vehicle’s provenance, pass intensive judging standards, and successfully achieve a record-setting final sale price of this magnitude.

#4648. CATL pushes ahead with 20 Ah solid-state EV batteries, with 500 Wh/kg in sight

CATL hit another milestone in its solid-state battery development, advancing to 20 Ah cells. The world’s leading battery maker aims to begin small-scale production in 2027.

CATL remains the leading global EV battery manufacturer by a wide margin. According to SNE Research, CATL held a commanding 39.9% share of the global EV battery market through the first half of 2026.

To stay ahead, the company is advancing several new battery chemistries, including solid-state and sodium-ion, promising to be safer, more efficient, and lower cost than traditional lithium-ion batteries.

When investors asked about the progress of its solid-state battery program on Tuesday, CATL said it continues to invest heavily in all-solid-state batteries and expects to begin small-scale production in 2027.

As it has stated before, output is expected to be limited at first as it scales up to mass production around 2030.

Speaking at the Summer Davos Forum in June, CATL chairman and CEO Robin Zeng said that, on a scale of one to nine, all-solid-state batteries have only reached level four.

All-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid-state batteries in that they require a solid electrolyte to conduct lithium ions, rather than a liquid.

The company uses a sulfide-based solid electrolyte system, which offers high ionic conductivity and deformability, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a hurdle.

CATL said its sulfide-based batteries have now entered 20 Ah trial production as it aims to achieve an energy density of 500 Wh/kg.

CATL’s 2027 timeline to begin small-scale production aligns with other automakers and battery manufacturers racing to introduce all-solid-state EV batteries.

Toyota, which has been promising solid-state batteries for nearly a decade now, aims to launch the first all-solid-state battery-powered EV in 2027 or 2028.

Using Sumitomo Metal Mining’s proprietary powder synthesis technology, Toyota claimed to have developed a “highly durable cathode material” for all-solid-state batteries last October. Toyota revealed a prototype last year, claiming it can deliver 745 miles (1,200 km) of range and charge in under 10 minutes.

However, like CATL, Toyota expects production to be limited and will not reach the mass market until closer to the end of the decade.

Samsung SDI, on the other hand, aims to begin mass production of its SolidStack all-solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027.

BYD, which ranks second in global EV battery sales behind CATL, also plans to launch its first solid-state battery-powered vehicle in 2027.

In an exclusive interview with Carwow.es last month, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD is in “the leading position” on solid-state batteries and will “prove that” next year.

BYD’s battery division, FinDreams, aims to begin producing sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries in limited batches in 2027, ramping up to mass production by 2030.

While solid-state batteries are often hailed the “holy grail” of battery tech, they are only one part of the equation.

It took them about 3 years for pilot to production of LMFP so I believe it. I generally believe CATL and BYD along with many of the others anyway. You can trust the big Chinese suppliers and OEMs on time line and what they have for the most part. Everyone else not a chance. I think Ford figured that out with suppliers.

CATL, BYD, and others continue advancing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion batteries, which will ultimately create more efficient, lower-cost options that offer various performance needs.

BYD’s second-generation Blade LFP batteries already deliver over 1,000 km (621 miles) of CLTC range. What’s next?

One thing is certain: New battery chemistries and evolving tech will only continue making EVs more efficient, unlocking longer driving ranges, faster charging speeds, and better performance.

#4647. Psychedelic nasal spray treats depression with toad-inspired goo

Published Oct 30, 2026 3:45 PM EDT

A powerful psychedelic compound best associated with the Sonoran desert toad (Incilius alvarius) has been recreated in a lab and transformed into a fast-acting nasal spray. A recent clinical trial outlined this week in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) suggests this spray could help people with treatment resistant depression, without the often less pleasant element of psychedelics. In the study, a single squeeze of the spray eased patients’ depressive symptoms with benefits lasting throughout the eight week trial.

Crucially, those long-term benefits (which have also been observed in other psychedelic research) didn’t require enduring an all-day mystical trip. Most patients were cleared for release less than two hours after taking the spray. Thankfully, the approach also eliminates the need to fondle a toxic amphibian. That’s potentially a plus both for patients and overharvested toad populations. The finds come amid a resurgence in new research and investment involving psychedelics, supported in part by evolving political attitudes towards the compounds on federal and state levels.

The nasal spray was developed by biotech firm AtaiBeckley. Its  active ingredient is called mebufotenin, which is also known as 5-MeO-DMT. The compound occurs naturally in several places, but it is most famously associated with the secretions of the Sonoran desert toad. For decades, amateur psychonauts have sought out these meaty North American toads for the prominent glands located on the amphibian’s head and hind legs. Squeezing those glands releases a milky secretion (sometimes inaccuracy referred to as venom), which when dried and then vaporized, produces an intense psychedelic experience. Many people who have smoked it describe a profound sense of oneness or ego dissolution, and some even report the sensation of dying.

Though based on the same compound, the drug in the nasal spray is synthetic and made in a lab. The researchers wanted to see if a controlled, clinical dose of 5-MeO-DMT could deliver some of the compound’s reported therapeutic benefits while keeping the overall treatment brief, especially compared with longer-acting psychedelics like psilocybin. They  limited their study to 193 adults between the ages of 18 to 75 with treatment-resistant depression. The participants, who came from the United States, Europe, and Australia, had each already tried at least two antidepressant treatments without success. By some estimates, around a third of all patients experiencing major depressive disorder also have treatment resistant depression.

Each participant received nasal spray in either a low (.3mg), medium (8mg), or high (12mg) dose. Neither the patient, nor the clinical staff or researchers involved knew which dose was given. The most intense psychedelic effects wore off relatively quickly, regardless of the dose. Clinicians checked on the patients at regular intervals to determine if they were deemed safe enough to leave the clinic. Among participants who received the 8-milligram dose, 85 percent were ready for discharge within two hours, compared with 78 percent of those who received the 12-milligram dose.

However, the therapeutic effects of the spray appeared to persist far longer.  Patients who received the medium or high dose showed significantly greater improvement than the comparison group as early as two days after treatment, and that advantage held through the end of the eight-week study. The team measured depression with a clinical scale measuring from 0 to 60, with  higher scores indicating more severe symptoms. After four weeks, the 12 mg group had dropped an average of 11.1 points on that score. The 8mg group dropped an even higher 12.5 points while the .3mg group dropped 5.5 points. These findings suggest the nasal spray application could provide some of the same therapeutic effects of other scheduled therapies less less need to have healthcare workers monitoring patients for many hours at a time.

“In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms,” the study authors write. “Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively.”

This experimental nasal spray arrives amid a transitionary period for psychedelic research. State governments have shown more interest in the field in recent years, with Oregon and Colorado each launching their own psilocybin programs. Even Texas, a state traditionally associated with a tough on drugs approach, just committed $50 million to research the powerful psychedelic ibogaine. Signs of movement are occurring at the federal level as well. In April, President Donald Trump signed an executive order aimed at accelerating research and FDA approval of psychedelic-based therapies.

Though it attracted significant attention, the executive order is really more signaling than action. It notably does not lower the bar a therapeutic needs to reach before archived FDA approval.

Still, pharmaceutical companies are clearly taking note. Earlier this year, Eli Lilly, the largest pharmaceutical company in the world, acquired AtariBeckley for $2.8 billion. AtaiBeckley developed the nasal spray used in the recent JAMA study.

#4646. Tesla’s rocket-shaped Robotaxi map in Houston is partly ‘fake’

Tesla’s new rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where the service won’t actually pick you up, according to Ethan McKanna, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker and former Tesla employee.

McKanna rode the service after Monday’s expansion and called Houston “by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area” he has seen. One trip quote had him spending about 40 minutes in a Robotaxi to go two blocks.

On Monday, Tesla expanded its Houston Robotaxi geofence into the shape of a rocket. It took the small launch zone in northwest Harris County and stretched it into a long corridor down to downtown and Bellaire, announced with “Houston, we have liftoff.”

McKanna runs Robotaxi Tracker, the crowdsourced site that tracks Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet and service areas, and he worked at Tesla this summer, so he knows the program better than most. He went to Houston to try it out. Here’s what he posted last night:

Another thing. Often AV service area maps advertised are kind of fake- they don’t actually go to everywhere in the polygon the provider publishes. Robotaxi Houston is probably by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area I’ve seenI get they were doing it so they could get… https://t.co/ILXIkmwGVp pic.twitter.com/yUfswZhQKF

The video shows the Robotaxi app with a pickup pin dropped in downtown Houston, well inside the polygon Tesla published. The app refuses it: “Location not available. Move the map to select a different location.”

McKanna acknowledged that AV service area maps are often “kind of fake,” since operators don’t serve every street inside the polygon they advertise. But he singled out Houston as the worst case he’s seen and said he understands Tesla did it “so they could get the starship shape,” which doesn’t seem like a good reason to fake availability.

The day before, he posted a trip quote that shows what this looks like for a rider:

40 min ride to cross 2 blocks downtown.this is pretty rough pic.twitter.com/n8kP4s9evT

The app quoted a 2:05 pm pickup on the east side of downtown and a 2:48 pm drop-off at Houston Police Department headquarters on Travis Street, a couple of blocks away. Instead of cutting across downtown, the planned route runs south through Midtown and the Museum District to the Texas Medical Center area, then loops back north.

McKanna’s read is that the Robotaxi appears to be avoiding railroad crossings downtown, and he said it fits with “other strange routing in Houston.” He expects Tesla to fix it.

To be fair, he wasn’t down on the service overall. He wrote that, apart from that issue, it “feels really good in Houston,” with reasonable wait times and “significantly better driving than my recent Waymo rides.”

Tesla isn’t the only one. On Tuesday, Robotaxi Tracker reported that Waymo’s Orlando service area had shrunk by 10 square miles, down 8.4% to 109 square miles. McKanna explained what happened:

Orlando’s airport was inside the map Waymo published, but McKanna checked the app and it won’t let riders set the airport as a drop-off yet. So the tracker took it out. Waymo’s airport service might be rolling out soon, and someone got ahead of the announcement.

That’s an airport on the edge of the map. In Houston, the dead zone is in the middle of downtown.

The key to understanding Tesla is the stockholders are the real customers, Elon looks at actual paying customers of his products as patsies or marks who will willingly serve as unpaid beta (or alpha) testers and who will be the ones paying or going to jail when something goes wrong.

First, a big thanks to Ethan. Tesla shares very little data about its Robotaxi program, and Robotaxi Tracker has become the best independent source on where Tesla’s fleet actually operates and how big it is. And as Orlando shows, he holds Waymo to the same standard.

Every AV operator has gaps in its map, Waymo included. But Waymo’s Orlando gap is an airport on the edge of the map that it’s likely about to add. Tesla’s Houston gap is downtown, and it drew a rocket first and figured out where the cars could actually go second.

Service and product should always outrank marketing, and that’s clearly not the case with Tesla’s Robotaxi. People rely on those maps to know if Tesla offers the service where they are. Faking the map just to make a rocket shape is completely stupid. Do better.

#4645. Verstappen Wins Mexico City Grand Prix over Hamilton and Antonelli

With his podium finish, Kimi Antonelli is the new F1 WDC Champion.

Max Verstappen wins his third Grand Prix of the year in Mexico City, ahead of Lewis Hamilton and the new World Drivers’ Champion Kimi Antonelli.

Verstappen won for the sixth time in Mexico City as Ferrari struggled, with another Grand Prix highlighted by a teammate battle.

On the opening lap, Leclerc took the lead from his Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton, who broke his three-year pole-less streak with his first pole for Ferrari on Saturday. Leclerc took the lead on the opening lap by pushing his teammate Hamilton aside. Verstappen followed through for second, and instead of giving back the position and falling to third, Leclerc held the lead and waited for his penalty.

Instead of the ten seconds his competitors expected, it was reduced to a minimum of 5 seconds due to mitigating circumstances.

On lap 44, just after Kimi Antonelli became the last driver to make their first pit stop, Valtteri Bottas experienced a suspension failure at 180+ MPH and slammed into the barrier outside turn one. The damage and cleanup brought out a red flag, leading to a second start.

On the restart, Hamilton took second from Leclerc after spending the red-flag period fuming, where he radioed, “We have big big problems,” about how Ferrari is handling it’s two racing stars and reportedly threw his scooter on the ground.

Verstappen held the lead on the restart and again on a safety car restart caused when Arvid Lindblad and Oscar Piastri collided while battling for seventh, sending Lindblad into the wall.

Lando Norris, the defending champion, battled Leclerc in the final laps to try and become the first driver off the podium as his fellow champions celebrated ahead, but settled for fifth ahead of the new champion’s teammate George Russell and his McLaren teammate Piastri.

With these drops, Isack Hadjar moves into ninth, and Ryō Hirakawa records a point in his first-ever F1 race in his last-minute appearance in place of Esteban Ocon.

#4643. Porsche Is Exploring a Way to Silence the Engine Drone in EVs

Kia's Telluride Is Closing In On The Sportage's U.S. Sales Crown

Ford Crams The Most Powerful OEM Crate Engine Ever Made Into New Bronco Concept

Mercedes-Benz Wants To Blow Snow Off Your Car Before You Open The Door

Porsche is poking around for ways to hush up range-extended EVs, and they’re not just stuffing more insulation under the carpet.

Dodge Unveils Six Turnkey HEMI V8 Crate Engines With Up to 1,025 HP

Cadillac Escalade IQ Has a Suspension Squeak With No Fix Yet

This 800-HP Ford F-100 Has Mustang DNA and a $1 Million Price Tag

Kia Leak Reveals Hydrogen Carnival, Next-Gen Sorento and EV7

Range-extended EVs are the awkward middle child between hybrids and full-on electrics. They roll around on electric motors, but there’s still a gasoline engine lurking in the background, acting as a generator when the battery needs a top-up. The idea is you get to cruise on electric power without sweating over where the next charging station is hiding.

But keeping a combustion engine onboard means you still get the usual suspects: noise and vibrations. Even if the engine isn’t hooked up to the wheels, it can still send a droning soundtrack straight into the cabin.

Porsche, never one to shy away from a technical puzzle, seems to have a workaround in mind. A patent that just surfaced shows a setup with both an electric motor and a combustion engine. The twist? Porsche wants to stick a two-cylinder boxer engine in the back as the range extender.

The patent was first discovered by CarMoses. Here’s where things get clever: instead of just piling on more insulation or fancy engine mounts, Porsche wants to use the electric motor itself to fight back against the unwanted engine noise and vibrations.

Think of it like noise-canceling headphones, but for your car. The system listens for the engine’s racket and then tells the electric motor to make just the right counter-move, tackling both the noise and the shakes that sneak through the car’s bones.

The setup involves a sound sensor in the cabin and a movement sensor near the engine, both feeding data to a control unit that decides how the electric motor should fight back against the noise.

Porsche even wants to preload the system with data about engine RPM and other conditions, so it knows exactly how to respond. If that’s not enough, they might throw in a shaker or a speaker to help quiet things down even more.

Unlike regular noise-canceling setups, here the electric motor pulls double duty as part of the noise-fighting team. In some cases, that means you won’t even need a separate gadget just to handle the counter-noise.

One possible application is a range-extended electric vehicle in which the combustion engine runs a generator instead of mechanically driving the wheels. Since the engine can operate at a relatively consistent speed, its noise characteristics could be easier for the system to anticipate and counteract.

That could mean less of the dreaded drone during long trips, when the gas engine has to keep chugging away to feed the battery. It also means a quieter, more refined cabin without loading up on extra soundproofing or complicated hardware. Letting the electric motor multitask could be a smart way to keep things simple.

For now, however, Porsche hasn’t announced a production vehicle featuring this technology. The patent also doesn’t establish whether the company intends to use the proposed arrangement in a future model or whether it is simply exploring the engineering possibilities.

As with other patent filings, the application and its publication do not guarantee that the technology will reach production. Automakers regularly patent ideas that may never make it beyond the development stage. All trademarks and brand names mentioned belong to their respective owners.

#4642. Kia’s PV5 electric campervan has two beds and a fully equipped kitchen [Images]

Kia’s electric campervan, based on the PV5, includes two double beds, a 200 W solar panel, and a fully equipped kitchen.

The PV5, Kia’s first 100% electric van, has been a huge success for the Korean automaker. After launching it at the end of last year, the PV5 has already become Europe’s top-selling small (C-segment) electric van.

Based on its modular skateboard platform, called E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to build custom configurations.

Although the PV5 is primarily sold in Passenger for everyday driving and Cargo for business use, Kia said the platform unlocks “endless possibilities” for different body styles and conversions, including a full-on electric campervan.

Wellhouse Leisure, a family-run campervan manufacturer based in the UK, revealed the Kia PV5 i-Camper.

The fully electric campervan is “now built and ready to view,” the company said. Based on the PV5 Cargo Plus, the campervan measures 4.69 m long, 1.89 m wide, and 1.99 m tall, which is about the size of a Ford Custom.

Although that’s pretty small for a camper, it offers more than you’d expect. Inside, the PV5 i-Camper includes two double beds with an elevating roof, a full kitchen setup, and a 200 W solar panel.

The sliding seat system enables the two rear seats to fold flat to form a bed and can be removed entirely. The upper bed, under the pop-up roof, has “more comfy” Froli Springs.

In the kitchen, you’ll find a sink with a tap and an electric water pump, two induction burners, a 42 L refrigerator, cabinets and storage spaces, and an optional microwave.

This EV would be a huge hit if imported into the US. Maybe after the huge order backlog has subsided Kia will consider importing the van to the States.

The vehicle also has a lithium leisure battery and a 12V supply, so you don’t need to use the vehicle’s main battery while camping.

It also comes with vehicle-to-load, letting you power external electrical devices, an e-bike, or even a campsite.

The PV5 Plus Long Range model uses a 71.2 kWh battery, providing a WLTP range of up to 247 miles. However, the added equipment will impact the range in the campervan conversion. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes around 30 minutes using a DC fast charger.

In the UK, Wellhouse Leisure lists the PV5 electric campervan starting at £63,000, or about $84,000.

#4641. Byron Wins Martinsville with Dominant Run as NASCAR Championship Battle Extends to Homestead

William Byron will not go winless in 2026, winning the season’s penultimate race at Martinsville and leading 362 of 500 laps.

Last year, William Byron won at Martinsville to secure his spot in what would end up being the end of the Championship Four. This year, he matched the win with his first of the season, but he will not be in contention next week at Homestead for the championship.

Byron’s championship hopes died a few weeks back when he fell out of mathematical contention, but the No. 24 Hendrick Motorsport team was still chasing a critical win to keep Byron’s six-year winning streak alive.

They delivered at Martinsville, where Byron led 367 of 500 laps, 300 more than the next-leading driver.

Byron took the first stage and lapped his Hendrick Motorsports teammate Kyle Larson, who is close to defending his 2026 championship with little help to his performance Sunday at Martinsville. He swept the stages, leading at the end of Stage 2 as the caution came out after Josh Berry spun Ryan Blaney.

Larson and Denny Hamlin, who entered the race 1-2 in the standings, both fell on the wrong side of strategy in the first stage and finished outside the points. More disastrous for Larson, he fell off the lead lap. Neither driver would grab a single stage point, while Bell, the only other driver in contention by the end of the race, finished fourth and 10th.

Byron had to hold off his Hendrick teammate Chase Elliott in the final stage as the No. 9 cut in on his lead.

“Chase is so good at managing his tires,” Bryon said on the front stretch. “I felt like I was going to have to do a really good job just to keep my tires happy through lap traffic. And the last two runs, everyone's car gets a little bit better towards the end and makes it harder to pass lap cars.”

Chase Elliott finished second for Hendrick, ahead of Ty Gibbs and Berry. Shane van Gisbergen matched his best oval finish with a fifth-place finish.

Denny Hamlin, who fell to third in the standings, finished sixth and is now 70 points behind Larson, making marginal ground. Bell finished tenth but, with his stage points, sits 67 points behind Larson.

Larson is nowhere near celebrating his championship early, knowing that anything can happen at Homestead and the points matter until the end. If Larson finishes third in the first stage, he secures the championship. His goal is to get points early and then be able to race all-or-nothing for a win in the finale.

“I mean, it all could have been a lot worse tonight,” Larson said. “So look at the positives from that. Go to Homestead next week with a comfortable gap, but still not locked up. So we'd love to get a couple of good first stages and then pound it in the third stage.”

#4639. Ford EcoBoost V6 Teardown Reveals The Cost Of Skipping Oil Changes

Kia's Telluride Is Closing In On The Sportage's U.S. Sales Crown

Ford Crams The Most Powerful OEM Crate Engine Ever Made Into New Bronco Concept

Mercedes-Benz Wants To Blow Snow Off Your Car Before You Open The Door

The engine in question came from a 2021 Lincoln Aviator with approximately 70,000 miles on the odometer.

The Best-Selling Hyundai SUV In October Wasn’t The Tucson

Dodge Unveils Six Turnkey HEMI V8 Crate Engines With Up to 1,025 HP

Cadillac Escalade IQ Has a Suspension Squeak With No Fix Yet

This 800-HP Ford F-100 Has Mustang DNA and a $1 Million Price Tag

Ford’s 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 is known for its V8-like low-end torque, and some of the brand’s performance models, such as the Explorer ST and Ranger Raptor, use it. The engine can be fairly robust, but with poor maintenance, even a dependable power unit is bound to suffer.

Case in point: This EcoBoost V6 from a 2021 Lincoln Aviator, the luxury counterpart of the Ford Explorer, failed and was acquired by Eric of I Do Cars as a core return. The engine reportedly received only two or three oil changes despite having already clocked about 70,000 miles. At that mileage, it should have undergone at least seven oil changes, based on Ford’s maximum recommended interval of 10,000 miles.

From the outside, the engine looked intact, which was fortunate, as inadequate lubrication can cause excessive friction, overheating, and potentially catastrophic engine failure. But on the inside, the valvetrain and chain-driven timing system looked grim, with an abundance of oil varnish and sludge. It looked far more worn out than expected for a five-year-old engine.

Given that the 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 uses direct injection rather than the dual-injection setup found in the 2.7-liter version, the intake valves had significant carbon buildup. For the uninitiated, a dual-injection setup also sprays fuel into the intake ports, helping clean carbon deposits from the intake valves.

Moving to the engine block, the cylinders showed signs of moisture, likely because the engine had been sitting outside. Debris circulating in the contaminated oil likely contributed to significant damage to the engine’s internal bearings. The failure culminated in a spun rod bearing on cylinder six, with bearing shavings also found in the oil pan.

With the EcoBoost V6 using a twin-turbocharger setup, it is more demanding to maintain than a naturally aspirated counterpart. Such a setup operates under greater thermal and mechanical stress, making proper lubrication and cooling crucial to getting the most out of its performance. After all, the cost of maintaining a luxury vehicle like a Lincoln should be part of the ownership equation in the first place.

The 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged EcoBoost V6 remains in use today, with Lincoln rating the 2027 Aviator at 400 horsepower and 415 lb-ft of torque. The Aviator was previously available as a plug-in hybrid, which made 494 hp and 630 lb-ft of torque, but was discontinued for the 2024 model year.

Volkswagen’s latest recall now extends to Audi, affecting nearly 13,000 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles globally. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity.

Earlier this month, Volkswagen issued a recall with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) impacting 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs, model years 2023 to 2026.

Official information from the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) revealed shortly after that several thousand more VW Group electric vehicles are affected worldwide.

In three separate recalls now under investigation by the KBA, 72,668 VW Group EVs were included worldwide, including 9,881 in Germany.

The recall affects certain batches of the ID. Buzz, ID.3, ID.4, and ID.7 models produced between 2022 and 2025, as well as Cupra Born models from 2022 to 2024.

On October 27, VW Group added another electric vehicle to the KBA recall database. The latest recall impacts 12,734 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles globally, including just one in Germany. In total, Volkswagen’s battery recall now affects 85,402 EVs globally.

In the letter sent to the NHTSA on October 23, Volkswagen Group of America said it was issuing a recall affecting 9,048 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles in the US model years 2024 to 2025.

The recall stems from the risk of the battery overheating and potentially causing a fire under certain conditions when charged to over 80% of its limit.

Volkswagen said in a safety recall report with the NHTSA that “certain charging profiles combined with a state of charge over 80% may trigger thermal propagation.”

While the root cause is unknown, Volkswagen urged owners to limit charging to 80%. Owners of affected vehicles received an email saying VW “intends to apply a temporary vehicle setting that limits charging to 80%,” unless they opted out by October 21.

The safety recall follows Audi’s Product Safety Committee being informed of battery thermal events involving other Volkswagen Group EVs that use the same batteries as the Audi Q4 E-Tron.

Following an internal investigation, Audi found the same battery and production characteristics as the impacted VW Group vehicles. Audi said the majority of these were produced for the North American market.

Audi is not aware of any claims, crashes, fires, injuries, or deaths associated with the Q4 E-Tron’s battery issue.

Owners in the US can take their vehicles to an authorized Audi dealer, where the dealer will run a diagnostic check on the battery. If needed, the dealer will impose a temporary state-of-charge limit to 80%.

Audi expects to mail out interim letters notifying owners of the safety risks on December 18, 2026. Additional letters will send additional letters once a remedy is available.

#4635. November skygazing: Planetary alignments, a supermoon, comet, and more

Published Oct 31, 2026 9:00 AM EDT

Autumn is here! The air is crisp, the leaves are falling, and the sky is alive. November brings a whole gamut of celestial phenomena for stargazing enthusiasts from a  planetary prom to a meteor shower that can explode occasionally into the most spectacular of sky shows, and  a comet that won’t return for 21 years Let’s get to it!

Mercury is generally difficult to spot. It’s our solar system’s smallest planet and is often lost in the sun’s haze. But in the middle of this month, this speedy boy is flitting in to join the party that Venus, Mars, and Jupiter are throwing all month. The three larger planets will be in alignment for all of November, festooning the morning sky just before  dawn. Venus will be in the southeastern sky, with Mars high in the eastern sky and Jupiter a bit lower, but also towards the east. And Mercury? Look low in the southeast, and it should be visible just before the sun emerges over the horizon.

As the month continues, Mars and Jupiter will edge closer and closer to one another, casting shy glances at one another across the sky like teenagers at a school dance. They’ll finally slide in for a waltz just before sunrise on November 16, where their conjunction in the eastern sky will be chaperoned by the bright star Regulus. Look to the east, but make sure you stop looking once the sun begins to peek its way into the firmament. No planetary conjunction is worth cooking your eyes.

And once the music stops and Mars and Jupiter will slip gracefully away, the fireworks will begin. The Leonids will be visible all month, but their peak is predicted for November 18. At that time, their radiant point—the point from which the meteors appear to emerge—will be right next to the two disengaging dancers in the constellation Leo. This shower usually produces 10 to 15 meteors per hour. However, in 1966 it exploded into one of the most spectacular displays of celestial pyrotechnics ever seen, with thousands of meteors visible every minute. So you never know what you might see!

This month’s full moon is the first of three consecutive supermoons. As per the ever-indispensable Farmer’s Almanac, it will reach peak illumination while below the horizon at 9:50 a.m. EST on November 24. When  actually visible, it’ll appear brightest on the evenings of November 23 and 24. This month’s moon takes its name from the industrious, dam-building rodents of North America, whose long summers of hard work start to pay off in November, when they retreat to their lodges to wait out the winter. Several other Indigenous nations have names that also refer to what animals get up to during the fall: the Tlingit call it the Digging Moon, to the Algonquin it’s the Whitefish Moon, while the Dakota and Lakota call it the Deer Rutting Moon.

The final event of November: a visit from Comet 161P/Hartley–IRAS. The space rock  will reach perihelion—the point at which it’s closest to the sun—on November 27. At that point, its magnitude will be about 12, which means you’ll want a decent telescope to spot it. The International Comet Quarterly suggests at least using a telescope with at least a 7.8 inch (20 centimeter) aperture. If you’ve got such an apparatus, look to the east-northeast, just above the horizon.

Remember that you’ll get the best experience gazing up at the stars if you get away from any sources of light pollution. You should also give your eyes plenty of time adjust to the darkness, and review our stargazing tips before heading out into the night.

I know there is a price for performance, but the prices that Toyota charges for performance brake pads are kind of ridiculous, borderline extortionate. In case you didn’t know, there is an OEM performance package that some special GR86s come standard with, and customers can opt into their deal when purchasing their vehicle brand new.

The performance package includes Sachs dampers and a Brembo big brake kit and costs as much as $2,020 on the base trim and $1,500 on the premium trim. That sounds like a great deal until you run out of brake pads. Remember this number because it will come in handy later.

While the performance package is already a steal of a deal from Toyota, the money that it will take to sustain that performance is something else. In a video posted by JamiesGarage1 (@JamiesGarage1 on YouTube), he found out through a customer’s GR86 with the performance package that Toyota charges ridiculous prices for Brembo brake pads and rotors.

How much, you ask? Well, for the front pads alone, the suggested retail price is $1,481.44. For the front brake rotors, each Brembo unit costs $521.25; multiplying that by two, we get $1,042.50, bringing the total for the parts alone to $2,523.94. Adding the rear brakes into the mix, the rear pads are $1,380, and each rear brake rotor is at a mind-boggling $562.20 per piece.

If, for some reason, your GR86 needed all four corners to get a rotor and a pad replaced all at once, you’ll be set back a total of $5,028.34, which is more than triple the price of the performance package from the configurator, and that doesn’t even include tax and labor costs. JamiesGarage mentioned those prices are retail, and shops can get these parts at a discount, but we’re still looking at a total close to $4,000. Like I said, ridiculous.

After watching the video, we decided to check online prices for the pads. It’s important to note that non-Brembo models will cost about a hundred dollars for either the front or the rear; however, the Brembo sets will still set you back about $992.16 for the front and $924.09 for the rear, as seen on Toyota Parts Deal. That’s more “reasonable,” but it also goes to show just how much of a steal the Toyota GR86’s performance package really is.

JamiesGarage even went on to recount his experiences in a Mercedes dealership when it came time to replace a Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren’s brakes. The total bill was estimated to be around $40,000, but that’s a car that costs over $500,000. That car’s brakes cost just as much as a whole GR86, and customers will be paying around 14% of its retail value to maintain the brakes.

On that note, it’s also important to know that Toyota doesn’t use high-end calipers either; instead, they’re four-piston fixed calipers paired with a 12.8-inch rotor in the front and painted red, while the rear is given two-piston calipers paired with a 12.4-inch rotor. No carbon ceramics to speak of here, just a normal Brembo system that’s similar to the old Subaru WRX STI or BRZ’s setup.

Alternatively, you can get aftermarket pads and rotors. A trip to the GR86.org forum and you’ll find that some owners have already hunted down some alternatives and given their recommendations. Though keep in mind that your vehicle’s warranty might be called into question.

#4633. Dems introduce new $15,000 EV tax credit bill that has no chance — and that’s a problem

Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) wants to bring back the federal EV tax credit and double it. His new bill, the “21st Century Vehicle Choice Act” (H.R. 10881), would offer up to $15,000 on a new electric vehicle and $8,000 on a used one, and it would make both credits permanent.

The problem is that the bill has virtually no chance of becoming law anytime soon. And if EV shoppers start holding out for it, it could end up hurting the market it’s trying to help.

Landsman introduced H.R. 10881 on October 22. It was referred to three House committees (Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce, and Natural Resources), and as of today, it doesn’t have a single cosponsor.

The big change is to the new clean vehicle credit, Section 30D of the tax code. Under the Inflation Reduction Act, the $7,500 credit came in two $3,750 halves: one for meeting critical mineral sourcing requirements and one for battery components. Landsman’s bill doubles each half to $7,500, for a maximum of $15,000.

It also deletes the termination dates. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act killed the new and used EV credits for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025, and the home charger credit after June 30, 2026. Striking those dates would revive all three credits with no expiration.

The bill doesn’t touch the rest of 30D. North American final assembly, the $55,000 MSRP cap on cars and $80,000 cap on SUVs, pickups, and vans, and the foreign entity of concern rules all stay. So the full $15,000 would only go to EVs that clear both sourcing tests, which has always been a short list.

The rest of the bill is reports. Commerce would deliver a “Vehicle Choice Report” on vehicle variety and ownership costs, and the Department of Energy would file five years of critical minerals reports.

The most interesting part is a DOE study of “gasoline super-users,” defined as the top 10% of light-duty vehicle owners by gas consumption. The study would map the regions where they’re concentrated and their 100 most-used routes, then track charger availability along those routes every year for five years. Coltura, which backs the bill, says the highest-mileage drivers spend over 10% of household income on fuel.

Republicans control both the House and the Senate, and they’re the ones who just repealed these credits. President Trump signed that repeal.

Even if Democrats flip the House and Senate in next week’s midterms, a bill restoring EV credits would still need to get through a veto. So realistically, nothing like this happens before 2029.

It’s also a rerun. Landsman introduced the exact same “21st Century Vehicle Choice Act” as H.R. 10046 on October 25, 2024, 11 days before that year’s election. It got zero cosponsors and died in committee. This version landed 12 days before the November 3 midterms.

This is where the bill can do real damage. EV buyers are extremely sensitive to tax credit timing, and the last year proved it.

When the credit was about to disappear, buyers rushed in, and Q3 2025 became the best quarter ever for US EV sales, with market share topping 10% for the first time. Then the floor dropped out. Hyundai’s Ioniq 5 sales fell 63% the month after the credit ended.

The market is only now crawling back. According to Cox Automotive, US EV sales hit 262,649 units in Q3 2026, up 6.1% from Q2 but still down 39.5% year-over-year, at a 6.4% share of new vehicle sales. Tesla’s Model Y and Model 3 still dominate, but Toyota, Rivian, and Hyundai are growing again.

That recovery is fragile. A headline promising “$15,000 off your next EV” is exactly what makes a shopper on the fence decide to wait a year or two.

And waiting gets you nothing. The new credits would only apply to vehicles placed in service after the bill is enacted, so there’s no retroactive payout for buying now. If you already claimed the credit once, you’d get $0 anyway.

Meanwhile, the deals on the lot are real. Automakers have been cutting prices to make up for the lost credit, like Hyundai, which cut the 2026 Ioniq 5 by nearly $10,000 on some trims.

At Electrek, our position has always been clear: we think EVs are a net positive and ICE vehicles have unpriced externalities. Therefore, we will take whatever we can get to encourage EV sales, but our preferred approach would be a carbon tax on ICE vehicles.

We’ve been clear that policy shapes this market. Killing the $7,500 credit is the main reason US EV sales collapsed. Consumers didn’t suddenly decide they hate EVs. So we’re all for bringing incentives back.

But this bill is messaging. It has zero cosponsors and no CBO score, and it dropped two weeks before an election, just like the identical version two years ago.

They should focus on rooftop and community solar tax credits and initiatives. With rising electric rates, helping people alleviate those would be vastly more popular than EV subsidies.

To be fair, some of it is smart. The lower income caps and the once-per-taxpayer limit go after the most common criticism of the old credit, that it subsidized wealthy households buying their second or third EV. And the “super-user” study is the best idea in the bill. Getting a high-mileage driver out of a gas pickup does far more for fuel costs and emissions than putting a low-mileage commuter in their second Tesla. If Democrats want to rebuild EV policy in 2029, that’s where they should start.

The problem is that people will hear the headline number. If you need a car now and an EV fits your life, buy it now and take the deals that are on the table. Don’t plan your purchase around a bill that has no path to passing for at least two years.

Will Democrats come back with a real, cosponsored EV plan before 2028? I don’t know, but I suspect that the US will continue to fall behind the rest of the world when it comes to EV adoption.

If you’re buying an EV, powering it with home solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero, with or without a tax credit. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs.
